stop_rules: Stop landmark discovery searching after the original linkage and gene-identification reports plus independent confirmation papers are captured and backward citation leads add no new discovery event.

Stop enzymology searching after kinase, ROC-COR GTPase, variant-specific effects, and their coupling are supported by convergent biochemical evidence with explicit controls.

Stop substrate searching after direct-site, endogenous, inhibitor-sensitive, and in vivo evidence is assessed for the principal Rab substrates and two consecutive refinements add no new validated substrate class.
Stop pathway searching when vesicle, lysosomal, autophagy or mitophagy, and relevant neural or immune-cell evidence can be linked to enzymatic outputs with model limitations recorded.
Stop challenge searching only after incomplete penetrance, nonmanifesting carriers, conflicting substrate or model findings, and human-translation limits each have at least one eligible source.

Stop the full retrieval when every requested section has supporting and limiting evidence, all included records satisfy the cutoff, and the final update query produces no material change to the mechanistic synthesis.

Search-plan execution, screening, anchor recovery, and effect conclusions remain to be performed; this output specifies the replayable retrieval plan.
exclusion_criteria: Exclude records that mention LRRK2 or Parkinson disease only in background text and provide no relevant genetic, biochemical, substrate, physiological, or limiting evidence.
Exclude purely computational predictions lacking genetic, biochemical, structural, cellular, biospecimen, or organismal validation.
Exclude secondary summaries from claim support when the cited primary study can be identified and assessed directly.
Exclude studies whose relevant evidence was published after 2024-12-31, using publication and correction metadata available in PubMed.

Exclude candidate substrates supported only by physical interaction or colocalization without evidence of LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation; retain them only as unresolved candidates when they materially qualify the mechanism.
Exclude duplicate publications of the same dataset from independent evidence counts while retaining linked reports for provenance.
Exclude retracted evidence from positive support and retain the retraction record as challenge evidence.
inclusion_criteria: Include PubMed-indexed primary human genetic studies that report linkage, segregation, association, ancestry-specific frequency, founder effects, penetrance, or phenotype for LRRK2 variants and Parkinson disease.

Include primary biochemical, structural, cellular, biospecimen, and organismal studies that directly test LRRK2 kinase or GTPase activity, variant effects, substrate phosphorylation, or downstream physiological pathways.

Include studies of candidate physiological substrates when they provide direct kinase evidence, an identified phosphosite, endogenous phosphorylation, genetic perturbation, pharmacologic perturbation, or orthogonal replication; label the specific support present.
Include systematic reviews and mechanistic reviews for terminology and primary-record expansion, while basing final mechanistic claims on traceable primary evidence.
Include null, negative, discordant, failed-replication, incomplete-penetrance, knockout, correction, and retraction records relevant to the strength or generality of a claim.
Retain all languages indexed in PubMed and record when assessment is limited by unavailable full text or translation.
Deduplicate at the canonical PubMed-record level while preserving every query occurrence, query_id, wave, and query-to-record link.
Escalate conflicts in variant classification, substrate identity, phosphosite assignment, or direction of enzymatic effect to full-text comparison and report the unresolved conflict explicitly.

plan.question_frame: Target-mechanism question: through 2024-12-31, what human genetic and experimental evidence links leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2/PARK8) to Parkinson disease, which disease-associated variants and populations define that relationship, how do kinase and GTPase-domain changes alter enzymatic activity and downstream biology, which physiological substrates have direct support, and what null, discordant, model-dependent, penetrance, correction, or retraction evidence limits causal or general mechanistic claims? Scope: PubMed-indexed literature from database inception through the as_of date; human genetics, pedigrees, case-control and population studies, biochemical and structural studies, cells, human biospecimens, and vertebrate or invertebrate models; all indexed languages, with English title/abstract data used for retrieval; outcomes include variant association, segregation, penetrance, kinase/GTPase activity, substrate phosphorylation, vesicular and lysosomal biology, neurodegeneration, and reproducibility. stop_rules: Complete all 12 planned PubMed query events in the specified retrieval-wave order unless PubMed is unavailable; record any unexecuted event and reason.

Stop expansion after two consecutive independently screened expansion passes add no decision-relevant genetic, enzymatic, substrate, physiological, or limiting evidence.
Stop when the maximum budget of 12 query events is reached and report budget exhaustion plus unresolved evidence gaps.
Stop earlier when additional PubMed retrieval cannot change the brief's conclusions, confidence grading, or stated limitations, with the rationale recorded.
Re-run the date-limited update query immediately before synthesis and exclude records whose applicable publication date exceeds the as_of date.
Fail closed on conflicting duplicate records, variant identities, or phosphosite assignments until the conflict is resolved or explicitly reported as a coverage gap.
